question.text: Speculative losses from commodity derivatives can be:

answer.text: Set off only against speculative profits — and carried forward for up to 4 years
Set off against any income including salary
Cannot be carried forward at all

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the Indian Income-tax Act, a speculative business is taxed separately from other businesses, and the conventional treatment is that a speculative loss can only be set off against speculative business profits — it cannot be set off against salary, capital gains, or non-speculative business income in the same year. The unabsorbed speculative loss can be carried forward for a limited number of assessment years (commonly cited as four), during which it can only be set off against future speculative gains. The Trap: Speculative losses are not freely set-offable against salary or capital gains, and they are not "no carry forward at all." Conflating speculative-loss rules with the more generous regime for non-speculative business losses (e.g., 8-year carry forward) is the typical error. Note: The specific speculative-loss set-off restriction and four-year carry-forward were not located in the cited Series XVI pages (p.126; p.181-p.182; p.187-p.189; p.94), which cover CTT, stamp duty, SEBI turnover fees, and GST in the tax section. The framing above relies on general Indian income-tax knowledge of speculative-loss rules rather than on a workbook citation.
